title: Right Order, Wrong Scale: When Your LLM Judge Gets the Level Wrong
summary: Claude Cowork moves its agent sandbox to the cloud, Reflection promises a 501B open-weight model, OpenAI's EU watermark comes with an API opt-out, and nearly 30% of new US STEM dissertations contain AI writing. The deep dive: an MIT audit of 33 LLM judges shows that ranking answers correctly says almost nothing about whether the judge gets acceptance rates right, and what to do about it.
shownotes:
Claude Cowork goes cloud-only: one sandbox per session, the desktop app brokers local file access
Reflection announces Beam, a 501B-total, 23B-active open-weight MoE, weights promised later this month; Aleph Alpha releases Kolibri
OpenAI turns on textGrain watermarking for EU ChatGPT users but makes it optional on the API; Anthropic marks Claude output worldwide
NBER paper: nearly 30% of 2026 US STEM dissertations contain AI writing, and those authors leave academia more often
Deep dive: Lyu and Thompson (MIT) audit 33 LLM judges against 45,796 worker ratings: right order, wrong scale, and how to validate a judge for the number you actually report
